questions.q: How should the HC-SR501 PIR's OUT pin be connected to the Raspberry Pi 5?
choices: Through a resistor voltage divider, because OUT outputs 5 V
Directly to a GPIO pin, because OUT is already 3.3 V-safe
To a 5 V power pin, the same as VCC
Only via a HAT, never to a bare GPIO pin
questions.explain: Although the HC-SR501 is powered from 5 V, its OUT pin already outputs 3.3 V logic, so it connects straight to a GPIO with no divider. This is the opposite of the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor, whose 5 V ECHO pin does need a voltage divider.

questions.q: Why is 'pir.when_motion = sound_alarm' written without parentheses after sound_alarm?
choices: Parentheses are optional and make no difference here
It saves typing and runs slightly faster
Without parentheses you point at the function so gpiozero can call it later; with them you would run it immediately and hand over its return value
Parentheses would turn it into a different function entirely
questions.explain: A callback is registered by name. 'sound_alarm' refers to the function so gpiozero can call it back when motion happens, whereas 'sound_alarm()' would call it once right now and store its (usually None) result, so nothing fires on real motion.

questions.q: Why does the HC-SR501 sometimes trigger falsely for the first half-minute or so after power-on?
choices: It is in its 30–60 second warm-up period while it calibrates to the room
The GPIO pin is faulty and must be replaced
The Pi has not finished booting
It needs a voltage divider that has not been fitted yet
questions.explain: A PIR needs roughly 30–60 seconds after power-up to settle and calibrate to the background infrared, and may fire falsely during that time. Keeping the alarm disarmed for the first minute avoids these false alerts.

questions.q: Inside a function, what must you do before reassigning a module-level variable such as the event counter?
choices: Nothing special — assignment always updates the outer variable
Declare 'global alarm_count' first, or Python treats it as a new local variable
Pass it in as a function argument every time
Wrap the function in a 'with' block
questions.explain: To change (not just read) a variable defined at the top level of the file from inside a function, you must declare 'global name'. Otherwise Python assumes you are creating a new local variable and the assignment fails with a NameError.

questions.q: When you move the log() helper into a separate file called alarm_tools.py, how do you use it from your main program?
choices: Copy and paste the function back into the main file
Run alarm_tools.py separately in another window first
Write 'from alarm_tools import log', with alarm_tools.py in the same folder
Install it with 'sudo pip install alarm_tools'
questions.explain: A module is just a Python file. As long as alarm_tools.py sits in the same folder, 'from alarm_tools import log' brings the log function into your main program, exactly the way you import from gpiozero or datetime.
